provenance.instrument: Zoning Ordinance of Cumberland Township of 2003 (Chapter 27 Zoning, Ord. of 11-25-2003, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 CU3685, 'Cumberland Township, Adams County, PA', so this is Cumberland township, Adams County. District use lists and development standards are text tables in Parts 4 to 10. No zoning attachment was seen on the chapter page. Floodplain rules are in 27-1102 and in Chapter 8. New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 05-26-2026.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.'
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit use. The words searched (accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, living quarters, guest house, tenant house, elder cottage, extended family, conversion) find no such use in the zoning chapter

Uses accessory to dwellings 'include but are not limited to' a private garage, carport, parking, pool, open space, greenhouse or garden storage building, pet shelter, home occupation, antenna, fence and heating or cooling equipment (27-1501.1). No living quarters are listed. The Zoning Hearing Board interprets whether a questionable use is permitted as 'similar to' or 'customarily incidental to' a permitted use (27-1902.4A). An accessory use must be 'clearly incidental to and customarily found in connection with' the principal use (27-201 'Accessory use')

A dwelling unit is 'Two or more rooms used exclusively for occupancy by one person or family, containing living, sleeping, cooking, and bath facilities' (27-201). A two-family dwelling is 'A building designed for and occupied by two families', as a twin or a duplex (27-201). A family allows not more than three members unrelated to all the others (27-201 'Family'), so two households in one dwelling unit are not a family

Two-family dwellings are permitted by right in R and RMH (27-502.1), in VMX and TND, and in MX on a lot existing before August 22, 2023 (27-602, columns placed by order). No section on converting a house to two units was found, and 27-201 defines no conversion, so adding a unit to a house in those districts is read as making it a two-family dwelling that meets the district rules. The tract and density limits differ: R 0.3 acre and 3.5 units an acre, RMH 2 acres and 9 units, VMX 10,000 sq ft and 4 units, MX 40,000 sq ft and 12 units, TND 100 acres and 4 units under the TND Ordinance of June 21, 2001 (27-503.1, 27-603, 27-607). Residences in mixed-use buildings are by right in VMX, MX, BP and TND (27-602)

R figures: at most 3.5 units per developable acre, a tract of at least 0.3 acre and a lot of at least 12,000 sq ft (27-503.1). Two units would need 24,892 sq ft by the density figure. Developable acreage is the gross tract or lot minus rights-of-way, utility easements, floodplains, wetlands, 50% of steep slopes over 25% and 25% of steep slopes between 15% and 25% (27-201). Lot area leaves out any existing or future road right-of-way (27-201 'Lot area'). Central water and sewer are required unless the residential lots are two acres or more (27-503.1 note). RMH allows 9 units a developable acre on lots of at least 4,000 sq ft in a tract of at least 2 acres. An R Cluster Overlay permits two-family dwellings on a 10 acre tract with public water and sewer (27-503.2)

A and AR permit only the single-family detached dwelling among dwellings (27-402). In A each additional dwelling a parcel is allowed 'shall be located upon a separate and approved lot whether intended for transfer of title or not' (27-404.4B). So a second dwelling on a house lot in A is not a listed use. Each parcel as it existed on January 1, 2003 may hold a set number of dwellings, 2 for 5.1 to 15 acres and more for larger parcels, each additional one on its own approved lot (27-404.4A, B)

Accessory buildings: at least 10 ft from each other and from principal structures (27-1501.3). In R and RMH accessory structures stand at least 10 ft from property lines (5 ft beside a non-residential district) and are at most 16 ft and 1 1/2 stories tall (27-503.1). In A an accessory structure is at most 20 ft tall, and in AR 30 ft (27-403). In A accessory structures stand at least 10 ft from a like-zoned tract perimeter, 35 ft from a residential district line and 20 ft from other district lines (27-403.1). The mixed-use districts set accessory setbacks from the tract perimeter as well (27-603)
Parking: two spaces per dwelling unit for a single-family detached dwelling and for a two-family dwelling (27-1302)

Floodplain (27-1102): the identified floodplain is the special flood hazard area on the FIRM of July 22, 2020. 'Freestanding structures, buildings, and retaining walls' are prohibited in floodplains, as are on-site sewage systems, private wells and manufactured homes (27-1102.9). Basements are prohibited (27-1102.16C(1)). New residential construction or a substantial improvement has its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation (27-1102.16A). In an AE zone without a floodway no new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank without a DEP permit (27-1102.4B(2)(b), 27-1102.18F). An unelevated accessory structure may not be used for human habitation, has no sanitary facilities and at most 200 sq ft (27-1102.16E). Variances go to the Zoning Hearing Board and may not raise the 100-year flood elevation in the floodway, or more than one foot in an AE zone without a floodway (27-1102.11). An existing structure in the floodway may not be expanded if it raises the base flood elevation (27-1102.18). The floodplain's permitted uses are a closed list with no dwelling (27-1102.8). A lot of record in the floodplain may seek a variance for some reasonable use (27-1102.12). A variance for an unelevated accessory structure of 200 sq ft or more needs a recorded nonconversion agreement (27-1102.16E(9)). Chapter 8 bars a variance for some accessory structures (8-702.1C), whose full text was not read

Steep slopes: in areas of steep slope a structure the district permits needs a conditional use from the Board of Supervisors, and in areas of very steep slope only listed conditional uses are allowed. No more than 33% of the steep slopes on a lot may be disturbed (27-1103.4, 27-1103.6, 27-1103.8G)

Variances: Zoning Hearing Board on unnecessary hardship findings (27-1901.1C, 27-1902.4C). No bar on a use variance was found. A special exception or variance expires without a building permit within 12 months, unless the Board says otherwise (27-1902.13)

Nonconformance: a structure that does not meet the district standards may be enlarged only if the enlargement meets all of them, 'including but not limited to, front yard, rear yard, side yard, lot area, parking, buffers, and height of buildings' (27-1701.2A). A nonconforming use may be enlarged by special exception up to 35% (27-1701.2B). Part 17 has no lot of record rule

Overlays: in the Airport Hazard Area Overlay an addition or new structure needs a PennDOT AV-57 obstruction review first (27-1401.5). The Neighborhood and Mixed Multi-Family Overlays permit multi-family and attached dwellings on tracts of 5 and 10 acres (27-1402, 27-1403). They are not a path for one added unit

Not read: Part 1, Part 3, Parts 7 to 10, Part 12, Part 16, Part 18, the rest of Part 19, 27-1103.9 onward, 27-1104, Chapter 8 Floodplains apart from a search, the TND Ordinance of June 21, 2001, and the parking fraction rule

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R)
value.conditions: A building designed for and occupied by two families, as a twin or a duplex. A lot of at least 12,000 sq ft and 80 ft wide at the setback line, a tract of at least 0.3 acre, at most 3.5 units per developable acre, side yards 12 ft each and 30 ft together (no side yard at a common wall), rear yard 25 ft, 25 ft from a local street, buildings at most 40% and impervious cover 50%, central water and sewer unless the lot is two acres or more. In the floodplain no new building is permitted (27-1102.8, 27-1102.9A), so there only a conversion inside an existing house can be considered. Two parking spaces per unit (27-1302)

Developable acreage is the gross tract or lot minus rights-of-way, utility easements, floodplains, wetlands, 50% of steep slopes over 25% and 25% of steep slopes between 15% and 25% (27-201)

In the floodplain no new building is permitted (27-1102.8, 27-1102.9A), so there only a conversion inside an existing house can be considered. Two parking spaces per unit (27-1302)

value.name: Two-family dwelling (VMX)

Central water and sewer are not required in VMX (27-603). value.conditions: Each parcel as it existed on January 1, 2003 may hold a set number of dwelling units, counting those there on that date: 1 for 5 acres, 2 for 5.1 to 15 acres, 3 for 15.1 to 30, 4 for 30.1 to 60, 5 for 60.1 to 90, 6 for 90.1 to 120, 7 for 120.1 to 150, and 8 over 150 plus 1 for each 30 acres over 150. 'Each such additional dwelling shall be located upon a separate and approved lot whether intended for transfer of title or not', meeting this chapter and the subdivision and land development ordinance, with limits by soil capability class. A single-family lot is 0.5 to 2 acres. This is a new lot, not a second unit on the same lot

value.condition: In floodplains 'Freestanding structures, buildings, and retaining walls' are specifically prohibited, as are on-site sewage disposal systems and private water supply wells. The floodplain's permitted uses are a closed list with no dwelling, and yards there may not hold 'any other structure'. An addition is the enlargement of an existing structure, which 27-1102.18 governs. A lot of record wholly or partly in the floodplain may seek a variance for 'some reasonable use', and no variance is granted for development that may endanger human life.

In the identified floodplain new residential construction or a substantial improvement has its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, and basements are prohibited. In the floodway no encroachment without a hydraulic study showing no rise and a DEP permit. An existing structure in the floodway may not be expanded if it raises the base flood elevation. No part of an on-site waste disposal system may be in the floodplain except in strict compliance with the rules. Work costing 50% or more of the market value of a structure is a substantial improvement. Variances go to the Zoning Hearing Board and may not raise the 100-year flood elevation in the floodway.

In an AE zone without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse', unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office.

In the floodplain an accessory structure that is not elevated 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', has no sanitary facilities and at most 200 sq ft of floor area. One of 200 sq ft or more below the base flood elevation needs a variance, and a granted variance needs a signed Declaration of Land Restriction (Nonconversion Agreement) recorded on the deed before the certificate of occupancy. Chapter 8 also bars a variance for some accessory structures (8-702.1C). Its full text is not on file. The same model text in other towns sets the limit at 600 sq ft. Ask the zoning officer.

no_variance.quote: No variances shall be granted for a proposed accessory structure
no_variance.note: Only the opening words of 8-702.1C were read. The size it sets was not seen

value.condition: On steep slopes a structure the district permits needs a conditional use from the Board of Supervisors, and on very steep slopes only listed conditional uses are allowed. No more than 33% of the steep slopes on a lot may be disturbed.

Near the Gettysburg Regional Airport anyone who plans 'to add to an existing structure' or to erect a new one first files PennDOT Form AV-57 with the Bureau of Aviation for an obstruction review at least 30 days ahead, before asking for township permits. If the review finds a penetration of airspace, the permit shall be denied, and a variance may be sought.
